coordinator_review: GPT-6 Astra checked consequential source paths and official protocol, plus documentation candidate locations. This is pre-edit triage, not independent review of edits.

findings.title: Authentication API reference omits prerequisites and borrowed-buffer contracts
findings.claim: One-line summaries identify operations without stating unlock prerequisites, supplied-key versus raw-password semantics, or key-buffer lifetime and clearing responsibilities.
evidence: src/Oath/src/OathSession.cs:644-652 requires nonempty key and outstanding SELECT challenge
src/Oath/src/OathSession.cs:693-695 consumes the challenge after successful validation
src/Oath/src/OathSession.cs:725-783 accepts access-key bytes for set/unset operations
src/Oath/src/OathSession.cs:788-835 derives internally for the retry helper and clears its derived array
Investigator: OathPasswordChangeTests.cs:73-175 demonstrates unlock-before-change/removal
YKOATH Instructions and SET CODE require authentication when a validation code is set
findings.disposition: Document normal derived-key workflow, UTF-8 password input, challenge/unlock prerequisites, and ownership through completion. Do not prescribe arbitrary-key support or an exact accepted-length restriction without E1 resolution.
findings.confidence: high for omissions and source behavior; nonstandard-key contract unresolved
findings.proposed_owner: documentation editor; SDK maintainer for E1

findings.title: DeriveKey reference retains development-transition history
findings.claim: Breaking change: password changed from string to ReadOnlyMemory<byte>; pass Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(password) and clear the array.
evidence: Current param/returns documentation already states UTF-8 and ownership
src/Oath/src/OathSession.cs:631-640 consumes supplied password bytes
findings.disposition: Use present-tense encoding/ownership guidance and move useful transition history to migration material. Do not imply clearing encoded bytes clears a preexisting string.
findings.coordinator_refinement: The original does not explicitly claim the string is cleared. Treat that point as avoiding misleading guidance, not a quoted false assertion. Do not add a generic security lecture.

findings.title: Host password derivation is described as hardware-enforced
findings.claim: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1(password_utf8, salt, 1000 iterations, 16 bytes) — dictated by hardware.
evidence: src/Oath/src/OathSession.cs:631-640 derives on the host
src/Oath/src/OathSession.cs:725-755 sends key/challenge/response, not password or iteration count
YKOATH SET CODE says the key is expected to be derived from a UTF-8 password, 1000 PBKDF2 rounds, SELECT ID salt, and 16 output bytes
findings.disposition: Describe the SDK's host-side derivation and YKOATH password interoperability convention. Preserve implemented algorithm and parameters; do not claim the protocol page explicitly specifies the PBKDF2 PRF.

findings.title: Password changes are grouped with irreversible credential deletion
findings.claim: Reset erases credentials/access key; DeleteCredentialAsync, SetKeyAsync, and UnsetKeyAsync are also irreversible.
evidence: src/Oath/src/OathSession.cs:725-783 changes/removes password protection, not stored OATH credentials
Investigator: OathPasswordChangeTests.cs:73-175 represents subsequent password changes/removal
findings.disposition: State specific effects: reset/deletion erase credentials; set/unset changes/removes protection. Avoid a blanket irreversible label or unsupported recovery promises.
findings.coordinator_refinement: Retain the fact that these operations mutate device state, but do not replace one broad warning with a new speculative recovery explanation.

findings.title: OathTool comment advertises absent remember/forget commands
findings.claim: Implements oath access subcommands: change, remember, forget.
evidence: src/Oath/examples/OathTool/Commands/AccessCommand.cs:19-114 implements ChangeAsync with clear option
src/Oath/examples/OathTool/Program.cs:55-82 dispatches change and help only
findings.disposition: Describe setting, changing, and clearing the access password via access change. Do not implement nonexistent commands to satisfy a stale comment.

findings.title: OathTool drops caller cancellation during password authentication
findings.claim: Session helper accepts a cancellation token but does not propagate it to password input/unlocking.
evidence: UnlockSessionAsync has no token parameter and calls reader/ValidateAsync without one
New-password confirmation also omits the token
Investigator: ConsoleCredentialReader.cs exposes token-aware interactive input
findings.disposition: Separate engineering follow-up to preserve cancellation through input, confirmation, and validation; do not document the omission as intended behavior.
findings.coordinator_refinement: Engineering work must also examine catch(Exception) cancellation handling; propagation alone may still convert cancellation to ordinary authentication failure. No runtime cancellation guarantee established here.
findings.deferral: User requested implementation review at pilot closeout; source evidence remains verified.

findings.title: VALIDATE raw response copy is not explicitly cleared
findings.claim: Repository policy requires clearing returned authentication material; the raw response copy containing the device HMAC has no explicit cleanup in ValidateAsync.
evidence: ApduResponse constructors allocate their own raw array; Data slices RawData
ValidateAsync clears expectedResponse, copied deviceResponse, outgoing data, clientResponse, and clientChallenge, but not response.RawData
Root CLAUDE.md:59-60 includes authentication material and secret-derived outputs in sensitive data
findings.disposition: Separate narrowly scoped cleanup fix and meaningful success/failure-path regression checks. Do not promise complete response clearing in documentation before the implementation is corrected.
findings.confidence: high for this raw-response array; transport copies, retention duration, and exploitability not assessed
findings.deferral: User requested implementation review at pilot closeout; source evidence remains verified.

findings.title: WrongPassword classification conflates distinct authentication failures
findings.claim: WrongPassword states the supplied password/key is incorrect, including on device-HMAC mismatch and status words 0x6984/0x6A80.
evidence: Device-HMAC mismatch independently triggers WrongPassword
SWConstants.cs:113,133 maps the caught constants to 0x6984 and 0x6A80
Official VALIDATE response codes label these Auth not enabled and Wrong syntax
Investigator: OathAuthenticationTests.cs fake maps incorrect keys to 0x6984; OathHashAlgorithmTests.cs hardware case expects any exception, not this reason
findings.disposition: Resolve error provenance and firmware status behavior before changing mappings or documenting them as definitive wrong-password evidence. Device-response verification failure should not automatically assert user error.
findings.confidence: high that multiple observations are conflated; intended classification and actual firmware mappings unresolved

escalations.question: Do public key methods promise only standard 16-byte password-derived keys, or a broader raw-key interface?
escalations.evidence: Only nonempty validation in code; protocol describes expected 16-byte password derivation.
escalations.decision_needed: Intended public contract and device constraints. No length change or broad support claim is authorized.

escalations.question: How should user-key rejection, failed device authentication, and syntax/protocol failures be distinguished?
escalations.evidence: Current shared WrongPassword mapping conflicts with the specificity of its prose and the protocol response-code descriptions.
escalations.decision_needed: Firmware-specific evidence, failure taxonomy, and whether a failed device verification invalidates the session.

escalations.question: Who owns the focused raw authentication-response cleanup fix?
escalations.evidence: Source-level omission confirmed by coordinator; repository policy already classifies the data as sensitive.
escalations.decision_needed: Implementation assignment and regression verification, not a prose exception.
